text: The delivery fact carries caseId, noticeRef, deliveredDate, deliveryStatus and barcode, and the notice answer of rwb-comms carries noticeId, caseId, state, sentDate, barcode, callBackDate and deliveryStatus; this story reads noticeRef and the delivered date from the fact and every other field from that answer.
why: The sources name the operations, the events and the Java interfaces but not the JSON element names of either row.
confirm: Contract review of RWB-P6-E1055-CON with the rwb-comms contract owner
impact: Renames only; no value, rule, criterion or test changes

text: A NOTICE_PERIOD timer has no warning point: warn_at and warned_at stay null, no MSG-P3-003 is sent for this clock, and the only output of the clock before its expiry is the due date on the case read.
why: No source read for this work package gives a warning point for a notice period, and the warning of the service is bound to the SERVICE_LEVEL row.
read: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 timer; RWB-P3-E1028-APP BR2; RWB-E1-055 section 8
confirm: Business lead and Legal at the wave 1 refinement
impact: One column stays null and one message is not sent; no criterion depends on a warning

text: The notice period is a legal clock: a deviation raised on the case pauses the SERVICE_LEVEL clock and leaves the NOTICE_PERIOD clock RUNNING with its started_at and expires_at unchanged, and the case record still shows the prescription date under MSG-P3-004.
why: R-DEV-01 names the prescription clock and Architecture v5 slide 3 says the legal deadline never pauses; the sources do not settle the notice period, and a statutory period counted from delivery is the kind of deadline a court relies on.
read: Architecture v5 slide 3 notes; R-DEV-01, R-UNI-43; RWB-E1-055 section 9
impact: The clock is never paused; if the ruling changes, one signal and one criterion change

text: The timer gains one nullable column, reference_ref varchar(40), holding the notice reference of the clock, with the partial unique index ux_timer_notice_running on (case_id, reference_ref) where timer_type = 'NOTICE_PERIOD' and status is RUNNING or PAUSED, and the expiry index ix_timer_notice_expiry.
why: The timer of the sources has no field for the notice it belongs to, and the clock must name its notice in the case pack; the field ID is not allocated in any source read here.
read: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 timer; RWB-E1-055 section 11; RWB-P3-E1028-APP section 13
confirm: rwb-case data owner and the Data Dictionary owner
impact: One column of 40 characters and two partial indexes in rwb_case; no other schema is touched

text: This story is the secondary rwb-case slice of RWB-E1-055 and owns no legacy criterion; the notice period from the P6 delivery fact starts here at wave 1, and the same clock from the S4 delivery answer is RWB-P3-E5002-APP at wave 3, with the partial unique index and the business key of notice and delivered date making the second fact a repeat counted under R-UNI-40.
why: The legacy story names the delivered date as the start of the clock and the Epics 3 to 8 set gives the same clock to another rwb-case story from another fact; the sources do not settle ownership between them.
confirm: TechX at the wave 3 refinement of RWB-P3-E5002-APP
impact: One clock per notice, one repeat path, no duplicate row

text: The expiry of a notice period is published as rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 with escalateTo taken from the escalation role of the SERVICE_LEVEL row in force for the case's queue and status, and a case with no such row expires with the role of the row that last applied.
why: No source read for this work package names a receiver for the end of a notice period, and the timers story of the service already carries the role on its SERVICE_LEVEL row.
read: RWB-E1-055 section 10; RWB-P3-E1028-APP BR3 and section 12.3
impact: One role on the event; no criterion depends on a named role beyond the SERVICE_LEVEL fixture

text: The platform contract stories named by the DP table (outbox and inbox, workflow kit, Flyway baseline, reference-data client, gateway-bff route) are in place from wave 0 and are not repeated as H rows, and the same-service reference-data and parameter contracts are wave 1 work of rwb-case; the metadata table therefore lists no build dependency, and this story is Day 1 against RWB-P6-E1055-CON and its fake.
why: The work package fixes the build dependency list as empty and the contract dependency as the one contract of the legacy key.
read: Template and Rules R5.4, R5.5, R5.7; RWB-P3-E1043-APP; RWB-P3-E1045-APP
impact: Ready to start Day 1; no build order changes
